notes: Identity independently checked: matching title Empathic-like responding by domestic dogs (Canis familiaris) to distress in humans: an exploratory study; authors Deborah Custance and Jennifer Mayer; DOI 10.1007/s10071-012-0510-1. Canonical text contains a ResearchGate cover followed by the original Springer Animal Cognition report, with Method, Results, Discussion and references; not merely an abstract or secondary report. No supplied PDF path, so no rendering available. Canonical parse encodes less-than p-bound glyphs as backslashes; literal quotes preserved and interpreted as p < 0.001. Printed requested F used without conversion. The three-condition composite ANOVA matches the description; component analyses, post hoc crying-versus-humming/talking p bounds, and crying-versus-silent-companion ANOVA are distinct tests. Candidate 18 dogs comes from Methods/scoring and the separate McNemar approach test (p. 5), not an explicit target-model N. No N inferred from df or summed. Replication and reported_success are unassigned placeholders.
